# openai_project_service_account (Resource)

Manage service accounts within a project. A service account is a bot user that is not associated with a user. If a user leaves an organization, their keys and membership in projects will no longer work. Service accounts do not have this limitation. However, service accounts can also be deleted from a project.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openai_project" "test" {
  name = "my-project"
}

resource "openai_project_service_account" "test" {
  project_id = openai_project.test.id
  name       = "my-service-account"
}

output "service_account_api_key" {
  sensitive = true
  value     = openai_project_service_account.test.api_key
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the service account. Updated in place.
- `project_id` (String) The ID of the project.

### Optional

- `create_service_account_only` (Boolean) Create without default roles or an API key. Defaults to false for compatibility. Existing built-in role grants must be removed before enabling the policy; existing keys are retained. Refresh fails if a role-free account acquires a built-in role.

### Read-Only

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) The API key that can be used to authenticate with the API.
- `api_key_id` (String) Internal ID of the API key. This is a reference to the API key and not the actual key.
- `created_at` (Number) The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the service account was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of the service account.
- `role` (String) The role of the service account. Can be `owner`, `member`, or `none`. Custom roles are managed separately.

## Least-privilege runtime accounts

Set `create_service_account_only = true` to create a keyless account with `role=none`, then grant a custom project role using the existing group membership and project group-role assignment resources. See the [runtime permissions guide](../guides/runtime-permissions.md) and [environment-independent example](../../examples/runtime-identity/main.tf).

Name changes use the supported update API. The API cannot update an existing built-in role to `none`; remove its built-in grant through the role-assignment API/resource before enabling role-free management. The provider blocks that policy change until the role is `none` and does not replace the account. Omitting the new argument preserves legacy state and key behaviour.

## Import

```shell
terraform import openai_project_service_account.runtime '<project_id>/<service_account_id>'
```

Import reads identity metadata and infers creation mode from the built-in role; it cannot recover an existing API-key secret or adopt group/role resources automatically.
